subject: Re: Dedicated capacity sizing - follow-up & GPU recommendation
messages:
From: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai>
To: Priya Shah <priya.shah@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Ashwin Kapoor <ashwin.kapoor@acmehealth.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 27 May 2027 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Dedicated capacity sizing - follow-up from today's call

Hi Priya / Ashwin —

Thanks again for the call today. Quick recap and next steps so we stay aligned on sizing for Dedicated capacity:

Call recap (high level)
- Primary workload: patient-facing summarization + clinical QA for inbound notes (low-latency per-request responses).
- Expected steady TPS: 10–15 TPS during business hours, occasional bursts up to ~30 TPS for batch jobs.
- Typical token mix: prompt ~150 tokens, completion ~350 tokens (avg ~500 tokens/req).
- Concurrency target: want ~50 concurrent requests headroom during peak.
- SLA expectation: p50 latency <250ms for short completions, p95 <800ms acceptable for longer completions.

Technical questions we talked about that will affect GPU sizing:
1) Preferred GPU family (H100 vs A100) — affects peak throughput and cost.
2) Whether batched steady-state inference is acceptable for some routes vs strict single-request low-latency for others.
3) Any strict data residency (you're in the US region) or VPC requirements (you mentioned wanting Private VPC down the line).

Based on today's inputs, I'm going to run a quick costing/sizing pass and propose two options:
- Option A (Performance-first): 4x H100 nodes, optimized for low-latency, supports sustained ~30–40 TPS with 50 concurrent headroom and KV/prefix caching.
- Option B (Cost-balanced): 6x A100 nodes with slightly higher batching to hit the same token throughput at lower cost, but expect p50 latency to be ~1.2x higher.

Can you confirm the following so I lock the numbers?
- Confirm avg tokens per request (~500) and burst TPS (30) are accurate.
- Is 50 concurrent headroom the right ask, or should I size for 75?
- Any routes that require guaranteed single-request low latency (no batching)? If so, which endpoints (summarization vs QA vs embeddings)?

I'll attach a first-pass capacity_estimate for you to review. After you confirm the numbers, I'll follow with a formal quote and a recommended rollout (canary -> ramp).

Thanks —
Rafael
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
rafael.mendes@redwood.ai
Attachment: capacity_estimate_acme_v1.xlsx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet)

From: Priya Shah <priya.shah@acmehealth.com>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai>
Cc: Ashwin Kapoor <ashwin.kapoor@acmehealth.com>
Date: Fri, 28 May 2027 10:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity sizing - follow-up from today's call

Thanks Rafael — great summary. A few clarifications from our side: 

- Avg tokens: yes, 150 prompt / 350 completion is accurate for our typical flows. There are a couple of long-report workflows (prompt 400 / completion 1,200) but those are batch and can be queued.
- Steady TPS: 12 TPS during business hours; bursts up to 30 TPS (rare).
- Concurrency: 50 is fine as the baseline. We might want to keep an option to move to 75 in future, but not required for initial procurement.
- Low-latency routes: Summarization (patient-facing) must be low-latency — no batching for that route. Clinical QA can tolerate batching up to 200ms extra.
- Residency: US-only is required; VPC option is desirable but we can start with Dedicated in our preferred region and evaluate Private VPC later.

Also: Ashwin, would your infra team prefer H100 or A100? Any internal constraints?

—Priya
Priya Shah
Head of Product, Acme Health
priya.shah@acmehealth.com

From: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai>
To: Priya Shah <priya.shah@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Ashwin Kapoor <ashwin.kapoor@acmehealth.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 29 May 2027 09:17:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity sizing - follow-up from today's call

Perfect — thanks for the confirmations, Priya. Based on that, here's a recommended configuration and rationale. I included the attached spreadsheet with line-item throughput math and a conservative cost estimate.

Recommendation (initial Dedicated pool):
- GPU: H100 nodes (4 x H100). Rationale: H100 gives ~1.6–2x inference throughput for transformer decoders on long context and mixed-precision execution, which maps well to your occasional long-report flows and the low-latency summarization route.
- Node sizing: 4 nodes provides steady-state ~12–15 TPS with room for caching/batching to hit burst ~30 TPS; supports ~50 concurrent in our simulation with p50 latency ~180ms for the summarization route (single-request path), p95 ~620ms.
- Batch strategy: Route-based policy — summarization set to single-request low-latency; clinical QA set to small batching (up to 8 requests or 200ms wait) which improves tokens/sec and reduces unit cost.
- Token mix: In sizing sheet I used 85% short flows (500 tokens), 15% long batch flows (1600 tokens).
- Autoscaling: Set min 3 nodes, max 6 nodes with scheduled ramps for business hours. That provides the 50-concurrency headroom and allows for an on-demand scale to 6 nodes for unexpected spikes.

Option B (cost-optimized) — if you'd rather: 6 x A100 with more aggressive batching on the QA route; estimate ~12% lower monthly cost but expect p50 latency for summarization ~220–240ms.

Next steps:
1) If this looks good, confirm we should proceed with Option A (H100) vs Option B (A100).
2) I'll produce a formal quote and a procurement-ready SOW (including migration/rollout plan and canary configs).
3) We'll schedule a technical handoff with an engineer (I suggest Aditya) to validate networking/VPC needs and test a small pilot.

Attachment: capacity_estimate_acme_v1.xlsx
Link: https://app.hubspot.com/deal/1234567

If you want, I can also run a short benchmark using a representative prompt set (we'll need an anonymized sample) — that will narrow the H100 vs A100 decision.

Best —
Rafael
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
rafael.mendes@redwood.ai

Subject: RE: Dedicated capacity sizing - follow-up & GPU recommendation

Looping in Aditya to prep the pricing/SOW draft and to book the tech handoff. Rafael — can you confirm target contract start date (we typically allow 2–3 weeks for procurement + 1 week for pilot/provisioning)? Priya — if you have a procurement contact, please share so we can get DocuSign moving when Rafael sends the quote.

Proposed timeline:
- Week 0: finalize Option (A/B) + quote
- Week 1–2: procurement approvals + DocuSign
- Week 3: provision Dedicated pool (3 node min), run pilot with 1000 sample requests
- Week 4: roll to production with autoscaling to 4 nodes and scheduled ramps

Aditya — Rafael mentioned a benchmark sample would help. Can your team run a quick H100 vs A100 microbenchmark if Acme shares a sanitized prompt set? We'll include that in the SOW as optional engineering effort (1–2 days).

Thanks —
Marissa Cole
Sales Engineering Lead, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai
